rules.when: The task is a separate read-only planning assignment: architecture, decomposition, acceptance criteria, or a design decision needed before implementation. It is not routine task coordination or implementation from an accepted plan.
rules.why: High reasoning belongs in bounded planning. Return a concise plan and stop before implementation.

rules.when: The task is narrow read-only reconnaissance, file gathering, a mechanical edit, formatting, a targeted rename, or another straightforward operation with clear acceptance criteria.
rules.why: Use the requested GPT-6 Luna worker at extra-high reasoning for routine work too. Do not silently substitute a low-effort or different-model worker.

rules.when: The task is scoped implementation or straightforward tests from a sufficiently clear accepted plan, without unresolved architecture. Execution workers use the requested GPT-6 Luna extra-high profile.
rules.why: Implementation uses GPT-6 Luna with explicit xhigh reasoning after planning has removed architectural ambiguity.

rules.when: The task is an additional independent review that the captain explicitly requested or the change justifies. Routine acceptance review of worker PRs is performed by the medium-reasoning manager itself and is not a worker assignment.
rules.why: An extra reviewer assists rather than replaces the manager's own review; return architectural uncertainty to the high-tier planner.

rules.when: The task is a conflict helper: merging a worker branch into the integration branch conflicts because workers edited the same code. Read every worker's version of each conflicted region, keep each intended behavior, and push one resolution.
rules.why: One worker cannot see the other workers' edits. The helper reads all sides and writes the resolution on a fresh GitHub branch.

rules.when: First escalation: the manager rejected a GPT-6 Luna xhigh worker's attempt at implementation or debugging, or the same finding survived two CHANGES REQUESTED rounds.
rules.why: Move up one model tier at high reasoning. Relaunch the same task so it keeps its worktree, branch, and PR.

rules.when: Second escalation: the gpt-6.1-sol high attempt at the same task was also rejected or left the same finding unresolved after two CHANGES REQUESTED rounds.
rules.why: Last step of the escalation ladder. If this attempt is also inadequate, report to the captain instead of retrying.
